title: R' Shimon, son of R' Yannai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: R' Shimon son of R' Yannai. He is mentioned in the Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat ch. 13, halakhah 7, where he said: 'I did not hear this from my father; my sister told me in his name.' And there, ch. 4, beginning of halakhah 2: 'R-Sh b-R said: I did not hear this from my father' — Hyman regards this as a scribal error and says it should read R-Sh son of R' Yannai. And in Moed Katan ch. 2, halakhah 2: Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Yannai harvested

his vineyard during the intermediate days of the festival; all the people saw him and harvested after him; in the following year he left it, and it dried up. In Moed Katan 12b the incident is brought concerning R' Yannai, and Hyman writes that from this it appears that he was the son of the well-known R' Yannai, teacher of R' Yohanan, who as is known was wealthy and had vineyards. He is mentioned in Esther Rabbah ch. 3, 12; Song of Songs Rabbah ch. 4, locator פת; (and so it should read in Bereshit Rabbah, beginning of ch. 75); Midrash Tehillim

ch. 124, section 5. Hyman states that he also had a son named R' Yannai, who spoke in the name of his father, in Bereshit Rabbah end of ch. 81, Vayikra Rabbah 21:2. And we find in Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 175a: R' Yannai in the name of R' Shimon son of R' Yannai says: 248 iron hooks did the Holy One, blessed be He, place upon the 248 limbs a person has, etc. And this statement is brought in the Old Midrash Shmuel,

end of ch. 21, and there it reads 'R' Yannai son of R' Shmuel bar R-Y'; Hyman says it should read 'of R' Shimon bar R-Y'. And in Yalkut Shmuel, remez 126, Hyman says it was copied mistakenly in the name of R' Shimon ben Yohai, when what was written was R-Sh-B-Y [abbreviation], and he is R' Shimon son of R' Yannai.

The whole printed notice spans volume III, pp. 1191–1192. The whole consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 13:7 passage has my father and my sister, and Moed Katan 2:2 names Shimon son of Rabbi Yannai in the vineyard account: the people saw him and followed, and in the following year he left it and it dried up. The Bavli parallel is directly present in Moed Katan 12b, beside Hyman’s supplied 12a; it names Rabbi Yannai, says others delayed harvesting the following year, and says he declared the orchard ownerless. These differences are not silently harmonized, and Hyman’s inference identifying the father remains his. The whole Vayikra Rabbah 21:2 passage gives Yannai in the name of Shimon berabbi Yannai and the 248 iron hooks homily; it does not prove a father-son genealogy. The whole consulted Krakow 1893 Midrash Shmuel 21 paragraph instead has Yannai son of Shmuel bar Rabbi Yannai and 248 fetters. Hyman’s SHOULD READ Shimon remains his proposed correction, without claiming the consulted edition is his exact ‘Old Midrash Shmuel.’ The exact Pesikta pagination and Yalkut 126 copying history have not been collated. The supplied פת remains unresolved, and the original R-Sh b-R and R-Sh-B-Y sigla are not automatically assigned to familiar namesakes. All Hebrew and current notes remain unchanged.
